answer: I would like to talk about the person I go to whenever I need to talk something through. The best listener I know is a close friend of mine, and it is a quality I value in her enormously. We met at university, where we were in the same tutorial group, and she now teaches at a school in Sirajganj, so we still meet regularly. In an age when most people are just waiting for their turn to speak, she gives you her complete, [[undivided]] attention. She puts her phone away, makes eye contact and never glances around the room while you are talking. When I talk to her about a problem, she never rushes to offer solutions; instead she lets me express myself fully first, which is surprisingly rare. She asks thoughtful questions that show she has genuinely been paying attention. What makes her such a good listener is her natural [[empathy]]; she seems to feel what you are feeling. As for how I feel about her, I always come away from our conversations feeling lighter, as though a weight has been shared. Last year, when I was unsure whether to apply for a master's degree abroad, she listened to me for an entire evening without once telling me what to do. I think being truly listened to is one of the most [[comforting]] experiences a person can have. Honestly, her ability to listen without judgement is a genuine gift, and it is a big part of why she is so [[treasured]] by everyone who knows her.

followUps.q: Are you a good listener yourself?
followUps.answer: I am getting better. My job has taught me to listen carefully, because students often reveal their real worries only if you give them time. But I still sometimes [[jump in]] too quickly when I get excited.

followUps.q: Why do you think some people are poor listeners?
followUps.answer: Often because they are distracted, particularly by their phones, or because they are more interested in sharing their own opinions. Listening properly takes patience and genuine interest in the other person.
